title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting, streaming stability
author: Aisha Patel
description: Implements parity with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions for parameter handling and response surface. This change adds: 1) full params mapping (temperature, top_p, n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, logit_bias) with backward-compatible defaults; 2) role-name handling to accept string roles and common role aliases and preserve role ordering; 3) stop sequence handling and logprobs propagation to match OpenAI semantics (per-choice logprobs + token offsets); 4) response formatting fixes for structured output and function/tool calling compatibility (tool invocation hints, function name+arguments in structured events); 5) streaming stability fixes: chunk framing, finalization markers, and retry-safe idempotent streaming patch; 6) extended e2e tests (sync and streaming paths) and SDK compatibility shims for python/typescript. Motivation: customers report subtle differences when migrating chat flows (roles ordering, stop tokens, and function-calling payloads) which cause regressions in downstream parsers and evaluators. This PR closes ENG-1942 and reduces migration surface for OpenAI-compatible apps. Checklist: - [x] Implement params mapping and canonicalization - [x] Add stop sequence + logprobs propagation - [x] Stabilize streaming framing and add idempotency markers - [x] Add SDK compatibility shims (python + ts) - [x] Add unit, integration, and e2e tests - [x] Update docs and upgrade notes - [x] Bench and perf review (no regression) Related: linear/ENG-2017 (streaming stability follow-up).

release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params mapping (temperature/top_p/n/presence/frequency/logit_bias), role aliasing and ordering preservation, stop sequence handling and per-choice logprobs + offsets, streaming framing stability and idempotent reconnects, structured output/function-calling compatibility. Backwards compatible defaults maintained. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration guidance.
notes: No breaking changes expected. Customers using exact binary streaming behavior should consult the migration guide; we tightened framing and added finalization markers to make streams deterministic. Coordinated with SDK teams to deploy compatibility shims.
